newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRAGUE PSE CHANGES BLOCK TRADE RULES.
newsitem.headline: PRAGUE PSE CHANGES BLOCK TRADE RULES.

text.p: The trading committee of the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) on Wednesday ruled that any direct block deal to be concluded at the bourse must first be offered to a minimum of 10 members of the PSE.
Spokesman Milan Vodicka said in a statement that the rule would take effect on October 21.

"Block trades, from October 21, will be concluded only in the case where no-fewer than 10 members of the bourse will have access to the offer, through which the auction principle of trade will be maintained," Vodicka said in a statement.
A large proportion of the bourse's total turnover each day is conducted through direct block trades, and analysts have complained about the transparency of the pricing on these trades.
The committee also said it would seek to reduce the number of shares traded on the bourse -- from the current total of 1,796 issues -- "to a usual level for developed markets".
The PSE began trading 1993 with newly privatised shares from the hundreds of companies involved in the government's vouchers-based privatisation programme.
